_meta.note: Hand-curated ingredient substitutions. dietary_notes lists which restrictions the SUBSTITUTE (not the original) satisfies — Phase 2.2 filters on this field, so it must be accurate. In particular: ghee still contains milk-derived butterfat and is NOT dairy_free despite being lactose-reduced; honey is an animal product and is NOT vegan.

substitutions.notes: Best in savory cooking; changes flavor and texture in baking.
Adds a mild coconut flavor; solid at room temperature like butter.
Closest direct swap for baking; check the label for milk derivatives, some margarines contain whey.
Only for baking; reduces fat and adds sweetness and moisture, changes texture noticeably.
Slightly nutty and thinner than dairy milk; not nut_free.
Creamier than almond milk, good in both sweet and savory dishes.
Highest protein of the common dairy-free milks, works well in baking.
Whips similarly to dairy cream; adds coconut flavor.
Lower fat than heavy cream, will not whip into peaks; still contains dairy.
Blend soaked cashews with water; not nut_free.

substitutions.ratio: 1 tbsp ground flaxseed + 3 tbsp water : 1 egg
substitutions.notes: Binding only, does not leaven; best for dense baked goods like muffins.
Binding only; check label for dairy_free status, varies by brand.

substitutions.ratio: 1 tsp baking soda + 1 tbsp vinegar : 1 egg
substitutions.notes: Leavening only, does not bind; use where the egg's job is to help the batter rise.
Binding, adds sweetness and banana flavor; best in quick breads and pancakes.
Nearly identical flavor; confirm the specific bottle is labeled gluten-free, as some tamari still blends in wheat.
Sweeter and less salty than soy sauce; reduce added sugar elsewhere in the recipe.
Designed as a direct swap; results vary by brand, especially in yeasted breads.

substitutions.ratio: 1:1 for quick breads, not yeasted bread
substitutions.notes: Not nut_free; denser and moister result, does not work for structured/yeasted baking.
Best for thickening sauces or in a gluten-free blend; gritty texture on its own in baking.
Slightly less rich; good in most soups and braises.
Adds umami depth; good substitute in risottos and gravies.
Nutty, cheesy flavor but not the same texture; will not melt or brown like parmesan.
Sharper and saltier than parmesan; still a dairy cheese, made from sheep's milk.
Not nut_free; texture is coarser than real parmesan and it will not brown.
Tangier and thinner; works in both sweet and savory uses.
Higher fat, similar tang; still a dairy product.
Good for coatings and toppings; confirm the cracker brand is truly gluten-free.
Use certified gluten-free oats if gluten-free status matters; oats are naturally gluten-free but commonly cross-contaminated.
Popular low-carb swap for coatings; not vegetarian.
Works better than cornstarch in acidic sauces; can turn slightly slimy if overcooked.
Needs double the amount and longer cooking to thicken fully; not gluten_free.
Adds mild coconut flavor and solidifies when cold, which changes texture in dressings.
Baking only; cuts fat substantially and adds sweetness and density.

substitutions.substitute: chicken broth with a splash of vinegar
substitutions.notes: Non-alcoholic; add 1 tsp vinegar or lemon juice per cup of broth to mimic acidity.

substitutions.substitute: white grape juice with a splash of vinegar
substitutions.notes: Non-alcoholic and noticeably sweeter; cut back other added sugar in the recipe.
More acidic and sharper, lacks lemon's fruitiness; good in dressings, less so where lemon flavor itself matters.
Very close acidity and flavor family; slightly more floral.
More acidic and fruitier than rice vinegar; dilute slightly with water if it overpowers.

substitutions.substitute: white wine vinegar diluted with a little sugar
substitutions.notes: Mimics rice vinegar's mild sweetness reasonably well.
Thinner and less floral than honey, but the standard vegan swap.
Sweeter and thinner than honey; reduce the amount slightly.
Tangier and slightly lower fat; still a dairy product, not dairy_free.

substitutions.substitute: cashew cream with a squeeze of lemon
substitutions.notes: Not nut_free; blend soaked cashews smooth and add acid for tang.

substitutions.substitute: milk with lemon juice or vinegar
substitutions.ratio: 1 cup milk + 1 tbsp acid : 1 cup buttermilk
substitutions.notes: Let sit 5-10 minutes to curdle slightly; still a dairy product.

substitutions.substitute: soy milk with lemon juice or vinegar
substitutions.ratio: 1 cup soy milk + 1 tbsp acid : 1 cup buttermilk
substitutions.notes: Soy milk is one of the few plant milks that curdles similarly to dairy; other plant milks work less reliably.
Tangier and lower fat; still contains dairy and egg is absent, but not vegan due to dairy.
Usually soy or aquafaba-based; very close in texture and use to real mayonnaise.
Adds distinct avocado flavor and green color; best in sandwiches, not emulsified dressings.
Press tofu well before cooking; absorbs marinade flavor rather than having its own.
Closer chewy texture to chicken than tofu; made from wheat gluten, not gluten_free.
Different texture entirely; works in curries, stews, and salads more than as a direct cutlet swap.
Portobello or cremini for umami depth; best in stews, ragus, and burgers rather than steaks.

substitutions.ratio: 1 cup cooked lentils : 1 cup ground beef
substitutions.notes: Good in tacos, bolognese, and shepherd's pie; softer texture than ground beef.
Closest texture match to ground beef among plant options; check the package, some blends add wheat.

substitutions.substitute: king oyster mushrooms, sliced into rounds
substitutions.notes: Mimics shrimp's texture surprisingly well when scored and seared; flavor is milder.
Best in flaked preparations like 'fish' cakes or tacos; mild brininess, not a fillet substitute.
Coconut bacon (coconut flakes, smoked paprika, tamari) gives crunch and smokiness, very different texture.
